subject: Post-demo: Concurrency & Latency clarifications + MAP items
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@quickpay.com>; QuickPay Platform Team <platform@quickpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Concurrency & Latency clarifications + MAP items

Hi Elena / QuickPay Team,

Thanks again for joining the demo today — appreciate the detailed walkthrough of your payment flows. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the performance targets you called out and propose a short MAP (mutual action plan) so we can confirm feasibility and next steps.

SLOs you emphasized:
- Latency: P95 generation (end-to-end, API) <= 200 ms for non-streaming inference on 1k-2k token prompts.
- Streaming: deliver first partial token within 80 ms of request start for real-time fraud hints, then steady-state chunking at ~50 ms intervals.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline concurrency requirement 150 concurrent model sessions, spike tolerance to 350 for 60s bursts.
- Cost/decision threshold: prefer a serving configuration that keeps per-1M-token spend below $XX (we'll align on exact target once you share monthly volume).

Immediate MAP (proposed):
1) Redwood to run a targeted smoke test matching QuickPay sample traces (Dylan) — 10/30
2) Infra validation: Marcus to confirm memory/kv-cache sizing for 350 concurrent sessions + streaming IO implications — 11/02
3) QuickPay to share 7-day sample trace and peak concurrency windows (Elena) — 10/29
4) Joint SLO checklist and cost envelope draft (Dylan + Lauren) — 11/04

Attachments: I attached a concise SLO checklist and the template for sample traces (quickpay_requirements.xlsx). Please confirm dates or flag if we should shift.

Decision criteria we agreed would move this to a pilot: P95 latency <= 200 ms for key routes in 80% of test runs, streaming first-byte <= 80 ms, and sustained concurrency handling at 150 with correct graceful backpressure above that with acceptable drop/fallback policy.

Thoughts?

Thanks,
Dylan
--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Soto <elena@quickpay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: QuickPay Platform Team <platform@quickpay.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:02:13 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Concurrency & Latency clarifications + MAP items

Dylan — thanks for the recap and the clear MAP. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 200 ms P95 is for the authorization hint route (avg prompt length ~600 tokens). For reconciliation jobs (batch), higher latency is acceptable.
- Streaming requirement: first partial token within 80 ms is our strong preference for the fraud UI — if the first token is slower, the UX degrades noticeably.
- Concurrency semantics: when we said 350 spikes, that is concurrent active sessions across two regions (us-east/us-west). Ideally the pilot covers a single region (us-east) but with the ability to scale to cross-region within 2 weeks.

I'll upload the 7-day trace to the Drive folder and confirm by EOD 10/30. Also attached a short doc outlining our internal cost target (see quickpay_requirements.xlsx).

One ask: can Redwood surface token-level cost breakdowns in the pilot console so our finance folks can validate the model?

Elena

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 09:14 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Looping in Marcus for infra sizing.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@quickpay.com>, QuickPay Platform Team <platform@quickpay.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:43:55 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Concurrency & Latency clarifications + MAP items

Thanks — quick technical readout below (summary for the MAP):

1) Concurrency & KV-cache
- 150 sustained sessions: comfortable on a single dedciated GPU pool using our medium instance profile with prefix caching enabled. We expect ~12 GB KV cache pressure (depends on prompt reuse).
- 350 60s spike: requires burst pool (autoscaling) + pre-warmed instances. We can architect an autoscale policy to target <30s warmup for additional instances, but cold-starts will increase P95 over 200 ms during ramp.

2) Streaming first-byte target
- Hitting 80 ms first-byte consistently requires two things: 1) small-ish initial token generation kernel and 2) network path optimization (edge egress + keepalive). We can get to ~60-90 ms in controlled tests for 600-token prompts if streaming chunk size is tuned to 8-16 tokens and we enable kernel-level optimizations.

3) Throughput/cost tradeoffs
- We can meet the per-1M-token cost envelope using int8 quantized serving for most routes; reconciliation/batch can use cheaper batch endpoints. Exact numbers depend on monthly throughput — send sample volumes and we'll produce a cost delta table.

4) Data needed from QuickPay to validate
- Representative 7-day trace (requests with timestamps, avg prompt len, peak concurrency windows)
- A minimal subset of routes to include in the pilot (authorization-hint, fraud-ui, reconciliation)

Next actions I propose: run a playback smoke test (Redwood) against the sample trace and produce a short report with measured P95 and first-byte distribution. I'll own infra validation and the report. Target delivery: 11/02 EOD.

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: infra-sizing-notes.txt (stub)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Concurrency & Latency clarifications + MAP items

Appreciate the quick responses. Confirming updated MAP dates:
- QuickPay uploads 7-day trace: 2026-10-30 (Elena) — received.
- Redwood smoke/playback test: start 2026-11-01, report by 2026-11-02 (Marcus) — in progress.
- Draft SLO checklist & cost envelope: 2026-11-04 (Dylan + Lauren).

I'll also open a HubSpot playbook entry (HS-84231) with the decision criteria and attach Marcus's infra notes + our SLO checklist. If the smoke test meets P95 <= 200 ms for auth-hint in >= 80% of runs and streaming first-byte <= 80 ms median, we move to a 4-week pilot. If not, we schedule an optimization sprint and re-run.

Small follow-up: Elena, would you prefer a Canary rollout limited to a fixed subset of your tenant IDs or an egress-filtered test pool? That affects our rollout plan.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
